I updated `meter.c` for SDK 89.0 (it was built against 88.2). I haven't compiled it, because only the two CSV tables are available here. One edit rests on an assumption I couldn't check.

My first attempt used a Python script, and the session blocked it because nothing can approve that kind of command. I redid the changes with the Edit tool, and they all applied.

**What was breaking and what I changed**

1. **`furi_hal_adc_configure` now takes a second argument.** The new signature is `(FuriHalAdcHandle*, FuriHalAdcScale)`, so the old one-argument call would not compile. I now pass `FuriHalAdcScale2048`. The CSV doesn't list the `FuriHalAdcScale` values, so I took that name from memory of the official firmware. I left a TODO on that line. Check the name against the real SDK header and pick the scale you want, because it sets the measurement range.
2. **`meter_legacy_format` is removed (status `-`).** The new table lists no replacement. I replaced the call with `snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "%.2f V", (double)meter.volts)` and added `<stdio.h>`. I also dropped the manual prototype, since it declared a function that no longer exists. If you relied on the old output format, check that this one matches, because I don't know what the old one produced.
3. **`cfw_meter_set_backlight_boost(2)` is gone.** It comes from `meter_extra.h`, which was copied from a community firmware fork. It isn't in either API table, so official firmware won't provide it and the link would fail. I removed the call and the `#include "meter_extra.h"`. The backlight boost no longer happens. If you want it, it needs an official API or a fork-specific build. I left `meter_extra.h` on disk, unused. You can delete it.

**Not broken**
- The timer functions, `view_port_*` and the other ADC calls have the same signatures in both tables.
- `meter_default_precision` is still present, and `meter.c` doesn't use it anyway.
- `internal_adc_calibrate` is already marked `-` in the old table, and the app doesn't call it.
- `furi_hal_adc_set_averaging` is new and optional. I didn't add it.

**Existing problems I noticed but didn't change**
- `meter_tick` can still be running when `furi_timer_free` is called. The tables don't list `furi_timer_stop`, so I didn't add a stop call. Check your SDK for it.
- `meter.volts` is written by the timer callback and read by the main thread with no locking.
- `text` is formatted but never displayed.
